validator: draft 1 fails one hard problem: whatAmILookingAt is 15052 characters, over the 12000 bound. Trim the card descriptions, the ripple strip and the SHOW screens' read lines.
keep: The idea up front: three single-phase transformers on one core; star or delta joins turn the output in 30-degree hours; the name records the joins and the hour; only matching ratios and groups may share a board, or the gap drives a circulating current.

The causal step is shown, not asserted: one flux per limb so the LV winding keeps time with its HV partner; a star's line voltage runs 30 degrees ahead of its winding's; a delta winding carries the line voltage itself; so Yy cancels to 0 and Dy lands at 11. The dashed limb-1 hands put that step on the clock.

Two cards as the brief asks: the clock with HV star/delta, delta closed A-B or A-C, and LV ends swapped (Yyn0, Dyn11, Dyn1, Dyn5, plus Yyn6 and Dyn7); and two units on an open switch, the gap arrow red unless zero.

Every figure computed from shown rules and checked: 254 V, 66.40 V, 6.63 and 3.83 turns per limb, gap 2 x 66.40 x sin(theta/2) = 34.37, 66.40, 132.79 V; circulating = gap share / (Z1 + Z2): 5.2, 10.0, 20.0 times rated at 5% each, 6.5 at 4%; worked example 502 A and 2610 A.

Typed answers for every figure (screens 1, 3, 5, 9, 11, 13) with want, slips and hints; options only for a direction (screen 7, Dyn11 ahead or behind) and for choosing between named units (screen 14).

Misconceptions caught: same voltage ratio is enough (screens 9 and 14, a Dyn11 and a Dyn1 both 440 V to 115 V); Dyn11's LV behind its HV (screen 7); line ratio taken as turns ratio with a delta (screen 5); one impedance counted for the circulating current (screen 11 slip 13).

Contested reading of Dyn11 handled plainly: 330 degrees clockwise lands where 30 degrees anticlockwise does, and the text says Dyn11 is sometimes described as a lag, so read it from the clock. Confidence simplified.

Footnotes only on what he would look up: 30 degrees an hour, Dyn11's letters and 330 degrees, 11 o'clock is a 30-degree lead, groups must match. No source named in a sentence. Generators deferred in one line.

shape: Matches the recommended shape: idea in one line up front, the rule in words, a worked example with real numbers (100 kVA Dyn11 beside a Yyn0: 34.37 V, 5.2 times, 2610 A), the misconception shown failing (same ratio, different group: 66.40 V gap), an analogy from his trade (battery strings in parallel) with where it breaks, practice with the safe way first, steps, rules of thumb and mistakes, and a recap he could say back.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with the four fixes.
